steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cream the softened butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy.
Mix in the lemon or orange extract, then gradually add the flour and salt until a soft dough forms.
Roll the dough into small balls, place them on the sheet and flatten each one slightly with a fork.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden.
Let the cookies rest on the sheet for 5 minutes, then cool completely on a wire rack.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cream the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, about 4 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla extract.
Whisk the flour with the baking powder and fold it in, alternating with the milk.
Pour into the pan and bake for 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease an 8-inch square pan.
Rub 1/2 cup flour, 1/4 cup sugar and 3 tablespoons butter together to make a crumb topping.
Cream the remaining butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs and coffee extract.
Fold in the remaining flour, baking powder and cinnamon, alternating with the milk.
Spread the batter in the pan and scatter the crumb topping over it.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and set in the center.
Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk the oil, sugar, eggs, milk and lemon or orange extract together.
Stir the flour and baking powder in just until combined; a few lumps are fine.
Divide the batter between the cups and bake for 18 to 20 minutes.
Mix the powdered sugar with the water and drizzle it over the warm muffins.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch round pan.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in the oil, milk and vanilla extract.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt until smooth.
Pour into the pan and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then on a wire rack.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk the oil, sugar, eggs, milk and coffee extract together.
Stir in the flour and baking powder until just smooth.
Fill the cups two-thirds full and bake for 18 to 22 minutes.
Cool completely before frosting, for example with a coffee buttercream.
Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C).
Beat the margarine and powdered sugar until smooth, then add the lemon or orange extract.
Mix in the flour and salt until the dough just comes together.
Roll out to 1/4 inch thick, cut into shapes and place on a lined baking sheet.
Chill for 15 minutes, then bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the edges just start to color.

name.fr: Crème au beurre à la farine (ermine)

steps: Whisk the flour into the milk in a saucepan and cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick like pudding.
Transfer to a bowl, cover the surface with plastic wrap and let it cool completely.
Beat the margarine and sugar until very light and the sugar is mostly dissolved, about 5 minutes.
Add the cooled flour paste one spoonful at a time, beating well after each addition.
Beat in the vanilla extract; the frosting should be silky and pipeable. Use it on cakes or cupcakes.
Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C).
Cream the margarine and brown sugar, then beat in the coffee extract.
Mix in the flour and salt to form a firm dough.
Press into an 8-inch square pan, prick all over with a fork and score into fingers.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, then cut along the scores while still warm.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until thick and pale, about 5 minutes.
Add the lemon or orange extract, then gently fold in the flour and baking powder.
Fold in the melted butter, cover and chill the batter for at least 1 hour.
Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter and flour a madeleine pan.
Fill each shell three-quarters full and bake for 9 to 11 minutes, until the humps rise and the edges are golden.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Cream the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs and vanilla extract.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, alternating with the milk.
Fill the cups two-thirds full and bake for 18 to 20 minutes.
Cool completely before frosting.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease two 8-inch round pans.
Cream the butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs one at a time and the coffee extract.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, alternating with the milk.
Divide between the pans and bake for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool, then sandwich and cover the layers with coffee buttercream.

name.fr: Gâteau aux agrumes à l'huile d'olive

steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch round pan.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale, then stream in the oil while whisking.
Whisk in the milk and lemon or orange extract.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until smooth.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes and dust with powdered sugar once cool.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk the oil, sugar, eggs, milk and vanilla extract together.
Whisk in the flour and baking powder until smooth.
Fill the cups two-thirds full and bake for 17 to 20 minutes.
These stay moist for days; frost once completely cool.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk the oil, brown sugar, eggs, milk and coffee extract together.
Whisk in the flour and baking powder until smooth.
Fill the cups two-thirds full and bake for 18 to 20 minutes.
Top with a mocha or vanilla frosting once cool.
Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cream the margarine and sugar until light, about 4 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the lemon or orange extract.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, alternating with the milk.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean, then cool on a rack.
Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cream the margarine and sugar until light, about 4 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla extract.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, alternating with the milk.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean, then cool on a rack.
Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cream the margarine and brown sugar until light, about 4 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the coffee extract.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, alternating with the milk.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean, then cool on a rack.

name.fr: Biscuits à la semoule et au citron

steps: Cream the butter and powdered sugar, then add the lemon or orange extract.
Mix in the semolina, flour and baking powder and let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet.
Shape into walnut-sized balls and flatten them slightly.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until pale golden underneath.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease an 8-inch square pan.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the yogurt, melted butter and vanilla extract.
Stir in the semolina and baking powder and let the batter rest for 15 minutes.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden.
Meanwhile simmer the sugar and water for 5 minutes, then pour the warm syrup over the hot cake and let it soak in.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, melted butter and coffee extract together.
Stir in the semolina, flour, baking powder and almonds to make a sticky dough.
Shape into two logs and bake for 25 minutes; cool for 10 minutes.
Slice diagonally 1/2 inch thick and bake the slices for 10 minutes per side, until dry and crisp.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch round pan.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then whisk in the oil, milk and lemon or orange extract.
Stir in the semolina, flour and baking powder and let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and springy.
Brush with a little citrus syrup or dust with powdered sugar.

name.fr: Gâteau de semoule à la vanille

steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch round pan.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then whisk in the oil, milk and vanilla extract.
Stir in the semolina, flour and baking powder and let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before unmolding.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch round pan.
Whisk the eggs and brown sugar, then whisk in the oil, milk and coffee extract.
Stir in the semolina, flour and baking powder and let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Serve with a coffee glaze or whipped cream.
Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cream the margarine and sugar until light, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Add the lemon or orange extract.
Fold in the semolina, flour and baking powder.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cream the margarine and sugar until light, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Add the vanilla extract.
Fold in the semolina, flour and baking powder.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cream the margarine and brown sugar until light, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Add the coffee extract.
Fold in the semolina, flour and baking powder.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and lemon or orange extract.
Knead for 8 minutes, then knead in the butter until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Shape into a loaf, place in a greased 9x5-inch pan and let rise for 45 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and vanilla extract.
Knead for 8 minutes, then knead in the butter until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Shape into a loaf, place in a greased 9x5-inch pan and let rise for 45 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and coffee extract.
Knead for 8 minutes, then knead in the butter until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Shape into a loaf, place in a greased 9x5-inch pan and let rise for 45 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30 to 35 minutes, until browned and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm water, oil, egg and lemon or orange extract.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Shape into a braid or loaf, place on a lined sheet or in a pan and let rise for 40 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden.

name.fr: Pain au lait à la vanille

steps: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, oil, egg and vanilla extract.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Shape into a loaf, place in a greased 9x5-inch pan and let rise for 40 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, oil, egg and coffee extract.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Shape into a loaf, place in a greased 9x5-inch pan and let rise for 40 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30 to 35 minutes, until well browned.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and lemon or orange extract.
Knead for 8 minutes, then knead in the margarine until the dough is smooth.
Cover and let rise for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces, roll into buns and let rise on a lined sheet for 40 minutes.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden.

name.fr: Petits pains sucrés à la vanille

steps: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and vanilla extract.
Knead for 8 minutes, then knead in the margarine until the dough is smooth.
Cover and let rise for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces, roll into buns and let rise on a lined sheet for 40 minutes.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and coffee extract.
Knead for 8 minutes, then knead in the margarine until the dough is smooth.
Cover and let rise for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces, roll into buns and let rise on a lined sheet for 40 minutes.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15 to 18 minutes, until browned.
Rub the melted smen into the semolina with the salt until every grain is coated, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
Knead the date paste with the cinnamon and a little orange blossom water until soft, and roll it into thin logs.
Moisten the semolina with the rest of the orange blossom water and the water, gathering it into a dough without kneading.
Flatten a strip of dough, lay a date log in the middle, close the dough over it and cut into diamonds.
Fry the diamonds in hot oil until golden, drain them, then dip them in warm honey and let the excess drip off.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt, then add the melted butter, egg, vinegar, orange blossom water and enough water to make a firm dough.
Knead for 10 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thinly, cut rectangles with a fluted wheel and make 4 slits in each one.
Thread alternate strips over a finger and fold them into the classic braided shape.
Fry until golden, dip immediately in warm honey and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.
Mix the semolina with 200 g of sugar and the melted butter, rubbing it between your hands until sandy.
Add 120 ml of water and the orange blossom water, mix, cover and leave to rest for at least 4 hours.
Spread in a buttered tin, score into diamonds and press half an almond on each.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for about 50 minutes, until deep golden.
Meanwhile boil the remaining sugar and water with lemon juice for 10 minutes, then pour the warm syrup over the hot cake and let it soak overnight.
Mix the almond flour, sugar, vanilla sugar and lemon zest.
Add the eggs one at a time until you have a soft, slightly sticky paste.
Shape walnut-sized balls and roll them in flaked almonds, pressing so they stick.
Bake on a lined tray at 170°C (340°F) for 15 to 20 minutes, until lightly golden.
Brush with warmed apricot jam for shine and top each one with a candied cherry if you like.
Whisk the oil with the powdered sugar and vanilla sugar until pale and creamy.
Add the flour gradually, mixing with your hand, until the dough just holds together and is very soft.
Shape small balls, place them on a tray and press a light pattern on top with a fork.
Bake at 160°C (320°F) for 15 to 18 minutes; they must stay pale.
Leave them to cool completely on the tray: they are very fragile while warm.

name.fr: Tcharek msakar (cornes de gazelle au sucre)

steps: Rub the smen into the flour and salt, then bind with orange blossom water into a smooth dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Mix the almond flour, sugar, cinnamon, egg and a little orange blossom water into a firm filling and shape small sausages.
Roll out the dough thinly, wrap each sausage in a strip of dough and curve it into a crescent.
Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 15 to 20 minutes, without letting them brown.
While still warm, dip them in orange blossom water and roll them generously in powdered sugar.
Make a smooth dough with the flour, salt, smen and water, then rest it for 1 hour and divide it into 16 balls.
Grind the almonds coarsely with the sugar and cinnamon, and moisten with orange blossom water.
Roll each ball paper-thin; layer 8 sheets in a buttered tin, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread the almond filling, cover with the remaining 8 buttered sheets, cut into diamonds and decorate with almonds.
Pour the rest of the melted butter over, bake at 170°C (340°F) for about 1 hour, then pour warm honey over the hot baklawa.
Rub the oil into the semolina until every grain is coated.
Add the sugar, vanilla sugar and baking powder.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and stir them into the semolina to get a thick, pourable batter.
Pour into an oiled tin and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden.
Cut into squares; serve as is or brushed with a light syrup or honey.
Rub the melted butter into the semolina with the sugar, salt and baking powder.
Add the milk little by little until you get a soft dough that doesn't stick; rest it for 10 minutes.
Shape small patties about 1 cm thick and coat them in a little dry semolina.
Cook on a hot dry pan over medium-low heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden.
Serve warm, split and drizzled with honey or butter.
Cream the butter with the powdered sugar and vanilla sugar, then add the egg.
Add the flour and cornstarch and mix just until a smooth dough forms; chill for 30 minutes.
Roll out to 4 mm, cut rounds and cut a small window in half of them.
Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 10 to 12 minutes, until barely golden, and let them cool.
Dust the tops with powdered sugar, spread jam on the bases and sandwich them together.
Mix the almond flour, 250 g powdered sugar, vanilla sugar and lemon zest.
Add the eggs and knead into a smooth paste; roll it out 2 cm thick and cut into squares.
Bake at 160°C (320°F) for 12 to 15 minutes; they must stay pale. Let them cool.
Make a glaze with the remaining powdered sugar, lemon juice and orange blossom water.
Dip the tops in the glaze, let it set, and decorate with small sugar flowers if you like.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, vanilla sugar and oil together.
Add the anise and sesame seeds, then the flour and baking powder, to make a soft dough.
Shape long logs, brush with beaten egg and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 25 minutes.
Slice the warm logs into 1 cm pieces.
Bake the slices again for 10 to 15 minutes, turning once, until dry and golden.
Cream the softened butter with the sugar and vanilla sugar.
Beat in the eggs, then add the flour and baking powder and knead briefly into a smooth dough.
Roll out to 5 mm and cut with decorative cutters (tabaa).
Brush with egg yolk and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 12 to 15 minutes, until golden.
Cool on a rack and store in an airtight tin.
Roast the peanuts, rub off the skins and grind them finely.
Cream the butter with the powdered sugar and vanilla sugar, then add the egg.
Mix in the ground peanuts and the flour to make a soft dough.
Shape small balls or cut shapes and place them on a lined tray.
Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 15 minutes and dust with powdered sugar once cool.
Whisk the flour, sugar, vanilla sugar and salt, then whisk in the eggs.
Pour in the milk gradually, whisking to avoid lumps, then add the melted butter.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes.
Cook thin crêpes in a hot, lightly buttered pan, about 1 minute per side.
Serve with sugar, jam, honey or chocolate spread.
Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a 20 cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together, then whisk in the sugar.
Whisk in the eggs one at a time until glossy.
Fold in the flour, cocoa and salt.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes: the center should still be slightly gooey. Cool before cutting.
Cream the softened butter with the brown sugar, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the flour, baking soda and salt.
Fold in the chopped chocolate.
Scoop balls onto a lined tray, leaving space between them.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 10 to 12 minutes; they firm up as they cool.
Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a loaf tin.
Mash the bananas, then mix in the melted butter, sugar and eggs.
Fold in the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt.
Pour into the tin and bake for 55 to 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and oil a loaf tin.
Mash the bananas with the oil, brown sugar and plant milk.
Fold in the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool completely before slicing; the riper the bananas, the sweeter the loaf.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a round tin.
Whisk the yogurt with the sugar, then the eggs one by one.
Add the lemon zest, flour and baking powder, then the oil.
Pour into the tin and bake for 35 minutes, until golden and springy.
Classic tip: use the empty yogurt pot to measure the other ingredients.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a 22 cm tin.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar and vanilla sugar, then add the melted butter and milk.
Stir in the flour and baking powder.
Fold in the peeled, thinly sliced apples; the batter should just coat them.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until golden and set.
Preheat the oven to 220°C (430°F) and line a 22 cm tin with crumpled baking paper.
Beat the cream cheese with the sugar until smooth, then add the eggs one at a time.
Stir in the cream, then sift in the flour and salt.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes: the top should be very dark and the center still wobbly.
Cool completely, then chill for at least 4 hours before slicing.

name.fr: Rochers à la noix de coco

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a tray.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar and vanilla sugar until frothy.
Stir in the coconut and let it soak for 10 minutes.
Shape small pyramids with your fingers.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the tips are golden.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and oil a 20 cm tin.
Whisk the flour, cocoa, sugar, baking soda and salt.
Add the water, oil, vinegar and vanilla and whisk until smooth.
Pour into the tin straight away and bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool completely; the vinegar and baking soda replace the eggs as the raising agent.
Cream the butter with the brown sugar, then beat in the eggs.
Mix in the flour, baking soda and cinnamon.
Stir in the oats and raisins.
Drop spoonfuls onto lined trays.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are golden.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 22 cm tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale and thick.
Fold in the almond flour and lemon zest.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and set.
Cool, then dust with powdered sugar.
Preheat the oven to 170°C (340°F) and line a 22 cm tin.
Melt the chocolate with the butter.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until doubled in volume.
Fold the chocolate into the eggs, then the cocoa.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes; it sets further as it cools.
Cook the butter until it smells nutty and turns light brown, then let it cool.
Mix the almond flour, powdered sugar and flour.
Stir in the egg whites (keep the yolks for another recipe), then the brown butter.
Fill buttered financier moulds three-quarters full.
Bake at 200°C (390°F) for 12 to 15 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden.
Heat the honey, sugar and a squeeze of lemon until it reaches a light caramel.
Stir in the sesame seeds off the heat.
Spread quickly between two sheets of oiled baking paper, 1 cm thick.
Cut into bars while still warm and let them harden.
Pit the dates and soak them in warm water for 5 minutes if they are dry.
Blend the almonds into coarse crumbs.
Add the dates and cocoa and blend into a sticky paste.
Roll into small balls and coat them in coconut.
Chill for 30 minutes; they keep a week in the fridge.

name.fr: Sablés à la farine de riz

steps: Cream the butter with the powdered sugar and vanilla.
Mix in the rice flour, cornstarch and salt until a soft dough forms.
Roll into a log, chill for 30 minutes and slice into rounds.
Bake at 160°C (320°F) for 15 to 18 minutes, keeping them pale.
Cool on the tray; they crisp up as they cool.
Stir the vinegar into the plant milk and let it curdle for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the oil, sugar and vanilla.
Add the flour, baking powder and baking soda and whisk until just smooth.
Fill lined cups two-thirds full.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 18 to 20 minutes.
